_doc: AIAS v1.20, final text (r1), locked by tag v1.20-prereg-r1. Pablo answered the nine pre-lock questions on Sat 2026-11-14 at 9:04 am CT (control panel: "Ok" to the recommendations); PRE_REGISTRATION_v1_20.md section 15 records them. Questions 1-6 are the six switches below: 'value' is what scripts/score_v1_20.py applies, records in every output and checks (it refuses a value outside 'options'). Questions 7-9 have no switch and are recorded under 'decisions': 7 and 8 fix the content of the cut list (scoping/cut_units_v1_20.csv), 9 does not apply.

Q1_study_id.effect: PHASE_ID of every output and the tag <id>-prereg-r1. Folder and file names keep v1_20.

Q2_scored_attempt.effect: first_counting: the first stored reply that counts under section 3 is the judgement (primary), v1.11-first is sensitivity S-ATT. v1_11_first (not chosen): the reverse (S-ATT primary, first-counting reported as sensitivity S-FIRST).

Q3_cap_cut_reply_invalid.decided: question 3, Pablo, 2026-11-14: true, a reply cut at the cap is invalid (v1.11's written rule)
Q3_cap_cut_reply_invalid.effect: true: a judge reply whose recorded finish reason shows the output cap is invalid even when it holds one complete object (v1.11 section 4.2 as written). false (not chosen): such a reply counts if its one object passes (v1.11's code).

Q4_reject_identical_objects.decided: question 4, Pablo, 2026-11-14: true, identical copies are invalid
Q4_reject_identical_objects.effect: true: two or more complete top-level objects make the reply invalid, even identical copies. false (not chosen): copies identical as JSON (same keys, same values, same JSON types) count as one object; different objects stay invalid.

Q5_cut_answers.effect: keep_r4: the primary analysis keeps answers cut at the answering model's output limit; S-CUT and S-CUT-M drop them, with the recognition-score floor n >= 4 there; F and E floors stay 6. Not chosen: keep_r6 (floor 6), drop_r4 / drop_r6 (the primary drops the S-CUT answers; the full set is sensitivity S-ALL).

Q6_case_b_result.effect: true: if v1.11's Stage J halts on JUDGE_FAIL (case B), v1.20's verdicts are Sentiment Paper A's result for the release decision (AIAS 4.0 in the current plan). false (not chosen): v1.20 is reported as a pre-registered re-scoring only, in both cases.
